  <div class="pub-title">Well-being salience in corporate disclosures and worker health</div>
  <div class="pub-authors">Di Francesco, R., Hull, P. &amp; Menon, S.</div>
  <p style="margin-top:0.6rem;font-size:0.9rem;color:#666;">We study how firms' orientation toward employee well-being&mdash;measured from the language of Danish corporate disclosures&mdash;shapes worker health. Exploiting workers' mobility between firms, we find that moving to a higher-salience employer raises sickness absence but not mental-health-care use, pointing to a behavioral rather than a health channel.</p>
